BMC buys former House of Seasoning building, further expanding its Pittsfield real estate

Berkshire Medical Center has purchased a former restaurant building to "expand access to care."

Tara Monastesse Tara Monastesse Pittsfield City Reporter
Published thursday, October 8, 2026 - 8:00 a.m.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:51
Instaread

PITTSFIELD — Berkshire Medical Center has purchased the former House of Seasoning restaurant building at 117 Seymour St., the fifth city property it has quietly obtained within the last year.

According to the state registry of deeds, the property sold for $300,000 on Sept. 18. The county’s flagship hospital system has now spent $1.26 million on expanding its real estate in Pittsfield since Dec. 31, 2025. 

It is not immediately clear how BMC will use the building. Jennifer Vrabel, executive director of BMC’s advancement office, said Berkshire Health Systems has “acquired some properties throughout the region, as we seek to expand access to care to create a more seamless experience for our patients.”
